finding: Each release batch is submitted with dist.batch_isend_irecv(ops), then the executor iterates work_handles and calls work.wait() before the next release batch. Requests inside a batch are submitted before waiting, but release batches are serialized by wait completion.
The executor uses frontier.commit_batch(limit=1), so timeline_light must measure whether many small release batches inflate submit_span_us and request_wait_us.
P0 full row matrix collection uses distributed all_gather and CPU materialization before planning. This is expected control-plane work, but it can contribute to pre-submit delay.
Plan agreement performs all_gather and broadcast plus CPU decode/materialization. These collectives are outside active P2P transport but can appear inside selected-layer hook wall time.

Async preflight runs collective validation for P0 hidden_states unless the plan/config selects local-only compact behavior. The next timeline must verify effective compact mode and preflight_collective_count.

Output tensor allocation and narrow views are created during phase execution. Static audit did not confirm per-task torch.empty allocation beyond the phase output, but pack/materialize timing is needed to separate allocation/view overhead from P2P wait.

Forward timing uses CUDA synchronization around measured forwards and computes checksum after forward. This is acceptable for comparable wall timing, but must not be interpreted as pure async overlap timing.

communication_makespan_us is computed from first transport submit to last transport complete across rank summaries. For selected P0/P1 it can include inter-phase gap and framework/expert/control time, so it must be reported as selected window span, not network busy time.
